project.name: Yetta
project.purpose: A future Windows 11 platform for deep customization and user-directed system management.
project.source_visibility: Public repository; source and project updates are published to GitHub.
project.license: Not selected yet. Public visibility alone does not grant reuse rights.

owner_requirements.scope_now: User explicitly requested the first Windows desktop program on 2026-11-14. Initial unprivileged prototype is allowed; do not enable system-modifying or privileged capabilities without a dedicated security review.
owner_requirements.publishing: Publish project source and relevant updates to the Yetta GitHub repository. Keep a changelog and verify public releases.
owner_requirements.security_priority: DAX and its privileged service are critical security boundaries. A compromise of DAX could expose the host to serious risk; minimize attack surface and avoid claims of absolute immunity.
owner_requirements.user_control: The user initiates commands and system changes. Yetta should provide tools and permissions, not autonomously modify the host.

application_concept.status: First unprivileged desktop preview implemented; privileged Access Manager, DAX and system-modification modules remain specification-only.

ui_modes.name: Windows 11
ui_modes.style: As close as practical to native Windows 11 Fluent Design and system settings.

ui_modes.name: iOS Glass
ui_modes.style: Custom translucent glass interface with blur, layered transparency, soft reflections, and owner-provided custom icons.

application_concept.shared_behavior: Both visual modes use one core, one settings model, one module system, and one Access Manager. Switching modes must not reset settings.

prototype.ui_stack: C# + .NET 10 + WPF, temporary; WinUI 3 remains an option for the future UI
limitations: No privileged helper, elevation or UAC bypass
No functioning DAX or Access Manager

access_manager.purpose: Unified subsystem to inspect, install, verify, and revoke Yetta's access profile.
access_manager.installation_model: The user explicitly installs a profile and grants the required Windows permissions once. Granted capabilities may be reused for ordinary operations until revoked or invalidated; the app should not repeatedly prompt for the same already-granted capability.

levels.name: Safe User
levels.description: Read-only inspection of files and system information within the actual Windows permissions available to the process. No write, move, or delete operations.

levels.name: User
levels.description: Normal permissions of the current Windows user account.

levels.name: Administrator
levels.description: Elevated administrator operations using supported Windows consent/elevation mechanisms.

levels.name: System
levels.description: Highest planned profile, backed by a dedicated hardened service and carefully scoped system capabilities. Requires future TTY authorization for critical actions.

access_manager.status_display: Show actual token, service, and resource capabilities; do not rely only on the selected profile label.
access_manager.revocation: Stop new privileged requests, invalidate active authorization, disable/remove the helper safely, and record success or partial failure.
access_manager.enforcement: DAX Guard denies an operation before execution when the active profile is below its declared minimum.

dax.purpose: Unified security and access subsystem. Internally divided into specialized workers; presented to the user as one coherent system.
dax.monitoring_scope: Only programs and commands launched through Yetta, plus their descendants. Do not monitor unrelated applications or perform machine-wide surveillance.
monitored_effects_where_attributable: file creation, modification, move, and deletion

components.name: DAX Process
components.role: Launch validation and descendant process tracking.

components.name: DAX File
components.role: File hash, signature, and reputation checks.

components.name: DAX System
components.role: Attribution of relevant registry, service, task, and driver changes.

components.name: DAX Threat
components.role: Microsoft Defender integration and optional threat-reputation sources.

components.name: DAX Update
components.role: Integrity and signature validation for updates.

guard.name: DAX Guard
guard.rule: Every Yetta-initiated operation must declare a minimum access profile. DAX Guard checks the active profile and denies execution when the profile is insufficient.
guard.fail_behavior: Fail closed if authorization, integrity, policy, or caller identity cannot be verified.

warning_types.name: Ordinary access request
warning_types.description: A resource permission request with Allow or Deny.

warning_types.name: Caution warning
warning_types.description: Unknown publisher, unsigned component, suspicious source, or uncertain reputation; user can inspect more details before proceeding.

warning_types.name: System-damage warning
warning_types.description: Warns when a user-requested action may damage Windows or disrupt operation; explicit Allow or Deny.

warning_types.name: Critical warning
warning_types.description: Highest System access requires future TTY (Trusted Token Yield) authorization and explicit user confirmation.

dax.warning_design: The owner will provide the visual design for each warning later. Yetta must not impersonate genuine Windows UAC, SmartScreen, or Defender dialogs.

virus_total.intent: Where possible, include VirusTotal reputation results in DAX logs when installing or moving files from removable media.
virus_total.upload_rule: Never upload user files automatically. Any future upload feature needs separate informed consent and an explanation that third parties may receive the file.

defender_and_override.owner_policy: If the active access profile is Administrator or System, the user may explicitly choose to continue after DAX 02/03 warnings, including a Defender malware detection, accepting responsibility. Guest, Safe User, and User cannot override.
requirements: do not bypass quarantine or Windows enforcement
use supported Windows/Defender restore or allow flows where required
defender_and_override.limitation: An application-level override cannot guarantee execution when Defender or Windows has quarantined or forcibly blocked the file.

tty.status: Planned; design later with the owner.
tty.intended_use: Critical authorization for the highest System access.

objectives: Protect the host from unintended Yetta operations
Protect DAX and its privileged service from misuse by other local processes
Limit blast radius if one component is compromised
controls: Signed binaries and signed update manifests/packages
OS-backed secret storage such as Windows DPAPI/CNG
Authenticated local IPC and strict caller identity checks
Strict request schemas, replay protection, and per-operation capabilities
ACL-protected service files, configuration, and logs
Dependency pinning and automated security checks
security_architecture.threat_model: Yetta and DAX are high-value targets. A compromise of the privileged service could expose the host to serious risk, so the service must have a very small, explicit API and never trust the UI blindly.
security_architecture.limitation: No user-mode application can promise absolute protection against a compromised Windows kernel or a fully privileged host administrator.

tamper_resistance.goal: Resist tampering by unrelated local programs and malware, while preserving the normal Windows uninstall path.
controls: Accept privileged requests only from an authenticated Yetta caller
tamper_resistance.uninstall: The supported Windows uninstall path must be able to stop/remove the service and clean up Yetta files and configuration.
prohibited: Blocking the owner or Windows from uninstalling Yetta
tamper_resistance.limitation: A fully privileged administrator or compromised kernel can still interfere with user-mode protections.

testing.current_phase: Infrastructure only; no Windows app to test yet.
planned_environments: Windows Sandbox for quick disposable tests
A full Windows 11 virtual machine with snapshots/checkpoints for deep system modifications
testing.isolation: Keep test VMs isolated from host files and credentials; do not assume Sandbox is a full clone of the user's machine.

Continue work directly through connected GitHub and Cloudflare tools; the owner declined a Work handoff.
Before modifying a repository, inspect its current state and preserve unrelated files.
Keep the website at https://yetta.pages.dev/ and deploy from Ketsuneban/Yetta main, root directory site, with no build command.
Keep all implemented-versus-planned status labels truthful.
Use the owner-provided logo at site/assets/yetta-mark.webp.
Keep DAX scoped to Yetta-launched processes and descendants, not all machine activity.
DAX Guard must block operations below the required access profile.
Remember the owner's Administrator/System override policy for warnings 02/03, while never silently disabling Defender or bypassing OS quarantine/enforcement.
Do not promise absolute security; document residual risks.
Update docs, changelog, validation workflow, and project continuity JSON when requirements change.
